chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the beard: if it is shaved and does not grow back, the wergild is complete; and if it grows back, it is a third of the wergild.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on compensation for shaving the beard?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential precedent set by Imam Ali (AS) regarding the variable compensation for beard injuries, distinguishing between permanent and temporary damage based on regrowth. It highlights the Shia legal principle that the severity of the wound and its lasting impact on the body's integrity directly determine the proportion of the full wergild (diyah) owed, reflecting a nuanced approach to bodily rights.
